29228.note: Family-owned St. Johns River fish camp off the Norris Dead River near DeLand with boat rentals, camping and cabins; food comes from the Marker 38 food truck.
29228.seas: Marker 38 food truck serves Friday–Sunday, 7:30 a.m.–2 p.m., during its winter stay at the camp.
29228.fn: The camp says Derris Rawlins founded it in 1962 and it marked its 63rd anniversary in 2025; it has since grown from 12 to 30 acres.

29637.note: New Smyrna Beach institution with a fine-dining room, a bar built into a live oak treehouse, and October 2026 events posted.
29637.fn: Norwood's says it has served New Smyrna Beach since 1946; no source confirmed the year at this address, so it is not listed as oldest.

29685.note: Riverside seafood shack on the Indian River Lagoon south of New Smyrna Beach, with kayak and paddleboard rentals and weekend live music.
29685.fn: The restaurant says John "JB" Bollman started it as a riverside shack in the late 1970s.

30049.note: Family-run Southern seafood house on the Halifax River where, it says, the servers are all cousins.
30049.fn: The restaurant says it has made its cinnamon rolls for over 45 years; no exact founding year given.
